ic_name: TIA/EIA-485 (RS-485 via TI SLLA272C Design Guide)

fsm_states_transceiver_half_duplex.name: TXR_DISABLED
fsm_states_transceiver_half_duplex.description: DE=0, RE#=1 — both driver and receiver tri-stated; transceiver in shutdown/low-power.

fsm_states_transceiver_half_duplex.name: TXR_RX_ONLY
fsm_states_transceiver_half_duplex.description: DE=0, RE#=0 — driver tri-stated, receiver enabled. R = digital reflection of V_AB.

fsm_states_transceiver_half_duplex.name: TXR_TX_ONLY
fsm_states_transceiver_half_duplex.description: DE=1, RE#=1 — driver enabled, receiver tri-stated (or echo-disabled). Bus driven differentially based on D input.

fsm_states_transceiver_half_duplex.name: TXR_TX_AND_LOOPBACK
fsm_states_transceiver_half_duplex.description: DE=1, RE#=0 — both enabled; receiver echoes the transmitted bit back to R (useful for half-duplex collision detection).

fsm_states_bus_logical.name: BUS_IDLE
fsm_states_bus_logical.description: No driver enabled; differential bus voltage near zero unless failsafe biasing pulls V_AB > +200 mV → all receivers see R = HIGH (mark).

fsm_states_bus_logical.name: BUS_MARK
fsm_states_bus_logical.description: Active driver pulls V_AB > +200 mV → all receivers see R = HIGH (logical 1).

fsm_states_bus_logical.name: BUS_SPACE
fsm_states_bus_logical.description: Active driver pulls V_AB < -200 mV → all receivers see R = LOW (logical 0).

fsm_states_bus_logical.name: BUS_CONTENTION
fsm_states_bus_logical.description: Two or more drivers enabled simultaneously — bus current spikes; data corrupted; relies on driver short-circuit current limit to avoid damage. MUST be prevented by software.

fsm_hints.direction_control_owner: Higher-level software (e.g. Modbus RTU master/slave timer, half-duplex tester FSM) owns DE / RE# scheduling.
fsm_hints.minimum_idle_before_TX: Higher-level protocols define inter-frame gaps (Modbus RTU: 3.5 character times) to guarantee bus quietness before next driver enables.
fsm_hints.DE_to_first_bit_delay: Implementation-specific transceiver propagation delay (typ 50..500 ns) — TX-side software must wait this delay after asserting DE before clocking data into D.
fsm_hints.last_bit_to_DE_deassert_delay: Transmitter must hold DE asserted until last stop bit has left the driver (otherwise the wire is tri-stated mid-stop-bit).

anti_deadlock_rule: Bus arbitration is NOT defined by RS-485 — collisions cause data corruption and rely on the application-layer protocol to detect and retry. Strict ownership rules at the application layer (Modbus master polling, time-division-multiplex, token-passing) substitute for hardware arbitration.
exit_from_reset: On power-up the transceiver power-on-reset (POR) holds DE = LOW (driver disabled). Software in the host MCU asserts RE# = LOW (receiver enabled) for receive-first half-duplex initial state. Failsafe biasing keeps R = HIGH (mark / idle UART line) so the host UART RX does not see a false start bit.

default_ready_state_recommendation.DE_default: LOW (driver tri-stated) — prevents bus contention during power-up before software is ready.
default_ready_state_recommendation.RE#_default: LOW (receiver enabled) — host UART RX sees idle mark, no false start bits.
default_ready_state_recommendation.Bus_idle_V_AB: > +200 mV (mark) by failsafe biasing, so all receivers report R = HIGH = mark.

loopback_diagnostic_mode.trigger: Set DE=1 + RE#=0 simultaneously on a single node while no other driver is active.
behavior: Transceiver drives V_AB according to D input.
Same transceiver's receiver sees V_AB and produces R reflecting D.
Allows software self-test of TX path + bus stub + RX path without external loopback wiring.

failsafe_biasing_modes.internal_failsafe: Built into modern transceivers; covers open-circuit / short-circuit / idle-bus; worst-case noise margin ≈ 10 mV.
failsafe_biasing_modes.external_failsafe: Resistive divider on each bus end (R_B in series with R_T); engineered for V_AB ≥ 200 mV + V_noise; restores robust noise margin.

isolation_recommendations: When ground-potential difference (GPD) may approach the -7 V to +12 V common-mode range, insert galvanic isolation (digital isolator + isolated DC/DC).
Direct connection of remote grounds via ground wire is NOT recommended (causes large ground-loop currents).
Resistor-bonded ground separation reduces loop current but leaves the link sensitive to induced noise.
Full signal + supply isolation provides multi-kilovolt GPD tolerance and is the recommended long-distance robust topology.
